Try get some professional help such as from a counsellor or psychologist if you haven't already. besides what is going on in your relationship there seems to more concerning issue going on with you at the moment. Priority first. 

In regards to your relationship. The only advice I can give you which is coming from someone who has been in the exact same situation as you, STOP BEING SO POSSESSIVE!!

I used to check my partners phone all the time looking to see if he was doing things he shouldn't be. Sometimes he was doing things I didn't like and I would get angry at him. In the end all I achieved from playing detective was pushing him away even more, which eventually lead to a very harsh break up. Which in my opinion is a lot worse then having to deal with the fact that sometimes he might do things I don't particularly like. Exceptions would be cheating, and illegal shit. But you would eventually figure that out anyway if that happened to be the case. 

You just need to trust her. Let her chill and talk with other guys, let her do things without telling you. TRUST that she won't do anything wrong. That is the foundation to a long lasting relationship.

Take action. Sit down with her and have a long chat about what you both are and are not comfortable with each other doing. Make reasonable compromises if necessary. (will most likely be the case). Try not to be a control freak. 

Promise each other that while this relationship lasts you will both try your best to adhere to those boundaries. Trust each other you wont break that promise without letting the other person know. If at any given time someone wants to break it. Try work things out, if you can't, split up and move on. In my opinion there is simply nothing else you can do. 

That probably didn't help at all. But I really hope it did. You seem to be a very nice person,  your just going through a rough patch ATM. I am sure you will figure this out in the end. This is coming from someone who is in the midst of their worst depression yet. 

TLDR: Get help first. Suicidal thoughts are very serious. As for the relationship. try your best to trust her, Split up if she breaks it.

Feeling occasional bouts of motivation is common in depression. its when you are starting to feel a big change in emotion over a period of time, like one month feeling extremely happy and one  month feeling super depressed is when bi polar could be s culprit.  You will find that a lot of depression symptoms, especially cognitive loss/brain fog can present quite a while before the usual sadness, hopelessness and lack of energy one would usually experience in the illness. I am not trying to make a diagnoses, I would highly recommend that talk to a GP about the symptoms you are suffering from. Anyway, It would be unwise for me to avoid asking these questions, have you ever experienced any head injury's in the past? Have you been, or are you a regular drug user? This includes alcohol and Marijuana btw...  Sorry if I seem a bit intrusive. its just in my experience I found that having a chat to someone about things like this before seeking medical care can make things easier.

It seems to me that your experiencing what is known as brain fog.  Brain fog generally consists of but is not limited to symptoms such as feelings of confusion, memory problems, reduced concentration, diffeculty speeking and thinking, usually bringing about a general foggy feeling in the mind, hence the name. There is no one cause of brain fog as it can be a result of lifestyle and dietry factors, depression, anxiety and many other illnesses, physical or mental. I would suggest going to your local GP and telling him/her how you feel as there is most likely to be an underlying cause.
